literal: Enmity called that which is devoid of any good quality, a person, even in jest, fit to be desired, is not.
translation: Enmity, which is entirely devoid of any good quality, is not something a person should ever desire, even in jest.
modern: நற்பண்புகள் இல்லாத பகை என்று சொல்லப்படும் தீமையை ஒருவன் விளையாட்டாகக் கூட விரும்பத் தகுந்தது அன்று.
explanation: This couplet warns against harboring or wishing for enmity under any circumstance. The poet describes enmity as 'பண்பு இலது' (that which has no good qualities), meaning it is an inherently destructive force that brings no virtue or benefit. Because of its toxic nature, one should not entertain thoughts of hostility even for amusement or in play ('நகையேயும்'). What begins as a joke or lighthearted rivalry can easily grow into deep-seated hatred and ruin lives.
